title: Sitting With It
logline: Every morning before the village wakes, a forest monk walks to the cemetery at its edge and simply sits there, the way he has for years, doing nothing that looks like very much.
human_question: What changes in a person who deliberately keeps death close, on purpose, every single day?

situation.what_happens: A monastic keeps a daily practice of going where the dead are and sitting there. It is unremarkable to look at and it has been going on for years. Around him the place does its ordinary work: a caretaker, a burial, families visiting graves, someone taking a shortcut. He sits. Then he walks back and the day begins.
situation.who_is_involved: The practitioner, whose training this is; the people who work at the place, for whom it is a job; the families who come there in grief, who are no part of anyone's practice and whose privacy governs the film entirely; and the lay community that supports the hermitage and has opinions about what he does.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the practitioner, whether the practice is doing what it is meant to do, which is urgency and less clinging, or one of the things the texts warn it can do instead: grief, satisfaction at somebody else's death, numbness or fear. For the film, whether a practice that produces no visible event can be shown at all.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A routine unfolds as repetition with small variations: the weather, who else is there, whatever he is carrying that week. It has no arc. It is interrupted by illness, by duties, by a funeral. Reality decides whether he says anything about it at all, and the honest ending is that whatever it has done to him cannot be seen from outside.

concept_merge.why_together: Recollection of death (C092) is the single concept here, and unusually it is already a practice rather than an analysis. The source separates four meanings of death and takes only one as the object; it warns that done unwisely the same reflection produces grief, glee, indifference or fear; and it directs the practitioner to charnel grounds and forests to see the dead and recollect wisely that death is certain for everyone, including oneself.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That keeping death in view is a skill with failure modes rather than a mood. The aim the source names is being shaken awake, and the benefits it lists are practical: less hoarding, less clinging, more care about doing harm, and meeting one's own end without terror. Watching someone do this daily shows the difference between that and both of its cheap alternatives, morbidity and 'you only live once'.

concept_links.why: The Pradeepika directs the practitioner to charnel grounds and forests to see the dead and wisely recollect that death is certain for oneself and for all beings, and in the same place warns that unwise recollection brings grief, glee at an enemy's death, indifference or fear [C092-P4:L80-L84]. Both halves belong in the film. The digest also forbids using the source's timely and untimely categories to explain or judge any real person's death, so nothing visible in or near the practice is interpreted, and the source's own remarks about the body and its humours are not presented as fact.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: The texts describe keeping death in mind on purpose, and wisely, as a practice meant to make a person more awake and less grasping, not gloomier. Done carelessly, the same thought only brings grief, glee, numbness or fear.
what_must_be_real: An established practice that exists without the film. Grieving families at the place are not filmed, and where they are present the camera is not. No claim is made about what the practitioner has attained. If he does not want to explain the practice, the film does not press him and does not explain it on his behalf.
position_hint: closing candidate: the group's calm, accepting note, and the one film in which its subject is faced deliberately rather than suffered.
risks: Presenting the practitioner as having attained something no camera can verify
Treating a working cemetery, and the people grieving in it, as scenery
Letting the film read as morbid, which the source itself names as the failure mode of the practice
drop_if: No practitioner with an established practice will be filmed
The place's use by grieving families cannot be respected while filming
Filming would turn the practice into a demonstration

connections.note: Someone whose working life is spent at other people's deathbeds gives a natural route into a private practice of recollecting death.
One watches a solitary practitioner keep death in view, the other watches many people training attention together.

selection.reason: Used by its episode and the group's only carrier of recollection of death.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
